Introducing Subscriptions to boost sales and retention for sellers on Dukaan

Conducted in-depth research and gained comprehensive understanding of stakeholders involved, delivering a solution that caters to user needs and aligns with business goals.

Product Designer

6 weeks, 2024
Platform

10kdesigners Capstone
Case study cover — Dukaan Subscriptions

Overview

Dukaan is a platform that enables local businesses to create and launch their e-commerce store without requiring any coding or technical skills. It's a B2B2C product, providing a platform for sellers to manage their online business while enabling customers to place orders on stores powered by Dukaan.

Currently, if a customer has to buy a product multiple times, they have to go through the checkout journey every single time, which is not a good experience and definitely not the best usage of their time.

The design brief: Design a feature for sellers/businesses to enable 'Subscriptions' on products — reducing friction for repeat purchases and boosting customer retention.

Understanding the Problem

Customer Shopping Behaviour

I conducted user interviews to gain insights into customer behaviour around purchasing items, their repeat purchase patterns, and the pain points they experience.

  • The frequency of purchases varies based on individual needs and consumption patterns.
  • Customers tend to stick with the same products and brands unless they've had a negative experience.
  • Quantity usually remains consistent, but varies when there are guests or specific occasions.
Key Pain Points

1. Keeping track of stock is difficult — customers only realize they need to restock when running out.
2. The constant need to repeat checkout is time-consuming and frustrating.
3. Physically going to the store for daily essentials feels tedious.

Key Decisions

02 decisions

Payment Method

I initially planned to keep Autopay only, but mapping the notification system revealed that for high-frequency orders, Autopay generates too many notifications — around 5–6 per day across WhatsApp, SMS, and email.

Design Decision

Introduced a Dukaan Wallet for high-frequency subscriptions (daily/weekly) alongside Autopay for low-frequency scenarios. This reduced notification overload and gave customers more flexibility.

Autopay flow
Wallet flow
Left: Autopay notification overload. Right: Simplified wallet-based flow.

Plugin vs Feature

Subscriptions are only relevant to a specific subset of sellers, and Dukaan uses plugins as a monetization strategy for optional capabilities.

Decision: Introduced subscription as a paid plugin rather than a built-in feature — keeping the core product clean while creating a new revenue stream.

Design Solution

Subscription Plan Creation

I followed Dukaan's existing design language to maintain consistency. The creation flow is broken into two clear steps: product selection and configuration.

Step 1 — Product selection with discount options

Frequency Selection

Research showed that the right frequency is critical — if the wrong options are given, customers won't subscribe.

Design Decision

Auto-selecting all frequencies reduces cognitive load for sellers, ensures customers always find a suitable option, and makes deselection a safer action than selection when the stakes are high.

Step 2 — Frequency, duration, and configuration

Product Selection Iterations

The initial iterations over-emphasized category-based selection, which didn't work because sellers' categories are often unorganized.

Iteration 1 — category-heavy
Final — search-first

Learnings

03 takeaways
  1. System-level thinking matters. Mapping the notification system early revealed constraints that changed the entire payment strategy.
  2. Default states are design decisions. Auto-selecting all frequencies was a deliberate choice to reduce risk.
  3. Research depth pays off. Understanding both seller and customer perspectives made the solution significantly more grounded.
